title: Simha and the Question Chain in Tempted to look at friend's paper during a test
storyText:
Simha gets stuck on a test question and can see a friend's answer nearby. Simha wanted to get the answer right. Simha does not know the answer and would have to look at someone else's paper. Simha stopped, caught on the question the moment had just raised: if "Cheating is okay if it helps me succeed." were true, would this really be as simple as it first seemed. Looking toward their friend answered nothing on its own — Simha does not know the answer and would have to look at someone else's paper was still there either way, and it only made Simha wonder something sharper: would taking the shortcut actually make getting to "get the answer right" go away, or just hide it for a moment. So Simha paused and asked the sharper question silently — if it came from their friend and not from Simha, would it actually be Simha's own. The answer came as a feeling more than a fact — one quick glance could solve the problem, which is exactly what makes the choice difficult that did not loosen no matter how Simha looked at it, as if some part of Simha already knew.

That left one question closer to the heart of it than either question before — not what would work, but what would actually make "keep an important secret until the right time" feel finished: the answer itself, or the way Simha got there. This time no new clue arrived from outside, not even a quiet hint of shelter. Simha already knew, quietly and completely, without needing anyone or anything else to say it first. All three questions folded into one another at once, and Simha understood: honest effort builds real confidence. Simha turned back to get the answer right and kept going, steady now instead of torn — not because the hard question had gone away, but because it was finally, fully answered.
